about.title: Trusted Legal & Investment Advisors Since 2011
about.p1: Aims Capital Associates is a corporate law firm licensed by the Rwanda Capital Markets Authority to provide legal and investment advisory services. story.title: Our Story
story.p1: Aims Capital Associates, established in 2011, is a corporate law Firm licensed by the Rwanda Capital Markets Authority to provide both legal and investment advisory services. The Firm, founded by Counsel Alloys Mutabingwa, FCIArb, is incorporated in Rwanda (2013), Tanzania (2015) and Delaware in the United States of America (2019).
story.p2: The Firm offers diverse services ranging from transaction advisory, legal services, contract management, disputes resolution, corporate services, tax advisory, Government relations, and project finance advisory.
story.p3: The firm has been commissioned to complete a review of over 50 Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) investment projects with an estimated total ticket size of US$610 million, aligned to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), Kyoto Protocol and Article 6 Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM) and Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) of the Paris Agreement. The review included verification of projects' conformity with UNFCCC CDM Standards, development of projects prospectus and pitch-book for COP28 due in November 2023. The Firm is currently working on an Investment prospectus for investment up-scaling in a US$100 Million Sustainable Housing Technology project.
story.p4: AIMS Capital was commissioned to jointly with GBRW and Garnet Partners successfully complete Rwanda's Five-Year Sustainable Finance Roadmap.
story.p5: Between 2018 and 2019, the Firm acting as a Consortium Partner with Tzamir Architects and Planners (Israel) and Horwath HTL, assisted the Rwanda Government in the development of Rwanda's National Land Use Master Plan (2020–2050) and the Presidential Order for its legal enforcement. The Firm reviewed the policy and legal framework for all land use and land development, including expropriation, investment, environmental management and the secular economy.
story.p6: In 2017, the Firm jointly with Planet Partnerships, commissioned by the African Development Bank, conducted a pilot study on waste management and circular economy across Rwanda, Ethiopia and Algeria.
story.p7: The Firm is the sole Advisor on Climate Finance and investment in Rwanda and a Professional Service Provider under the Kigali International Financial Centre (KIFC) framework. The Firm is a member of the Rwanda Capital Markets Authority (CMA) and the Rwanda Bar Association.
story.p8: Commissioned by the Rwanda Government under World Bank funding, the Firm developed a legal structure for the corporatization of Rwanda's Energy, Water and Sanitation Authority (EWSA). The successful outcomes of the assignment led to the formation of REG (Rwanda Energy Group) and WASAC (Water and Sanitation Corporation), with the Firm assisting through their formative stages ranging from writing governance instruments, separation of assets, and recruitment of skilled personnel.
story.p9: The Firm advised on the Bugesera Public-Private Partnership (PPP) water project — one of sub-Saharan Africa's largest known Build, Operate and Supply water deals. The US$63 million project delivers 40 million litres of water daily, growing Kigali's existing water capacity by a third. Financed through a blended finance model by the Emerging Africa Infrastructure Fund (EAIF), the African Development Bank (AfDB), and Metito (Emirates).
story.p10: In the aviation sector, the Firm is a leading advisor in transactions relating to sale, lease and Maintenance, Repair, Overhaul (MRO) contracts. The Firm holds a Service Level Agreement with Nexus Group (Saudi Arabia) and works closely with Avia Group (Vilnius) on aircraft transactions. The Firm has also entered into a representation agreement with Zhong Tong Group (China) — the largest manufacturer of buses including electric buses and their charging systems — to promote green technology in public transport across Africa.
story.p11: Despite the Firm's market vibrancy, it desires to increase its market share through affordable services. It works towards cutting a niche for itself in the market through its unique package of services that are so essential to clients, presenting the Firm as a sole reference for critical and high demand investment and business transactions.

hero.title: Projects
hero.subhead: Major advisory engagements and infrastructure projects delivered across Rwanda and the region

items.waterD: Advisory on the Kanzenze Water Treatment Plant / Kigali Bulk Water Supply Project — the first competitively tendered Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) bulk water concession in sub-Saharan Africa (outside South Africa). The plant, located in Kanzenze, Ntarama Sector, Bugesera District, was developed by Kigali Water Limited (KWL), wholly owned subsidiary of Metito (Dubai-based, 60+ years experience, 3,000+ facilities worldwide). Financial close: November 2017. Operational since 10 February 2021, the 40,000 m³/day (40 million litres/day) plant supplies 30,000 m³/day to Kigali and 10,000 m³/day to Bugesera. Financed through a 27-year BOT concession with EAIF ($19M senior + $2.6M junior debt), African Development Bank ($19M senior debt — all 18-year term loans), and Metito equity, backed by a MIGA (World Bank Group) guarantee. IFC acted as PPP transaction advisor to the Government of Rwanda. Counsel Alloys Mutabingwa, FCIArb, served as senior legal advisor on behalf of the Rwanda Government. Aims Capital's advisory on government participation in forwarding infrastructure was key to making the tariff commercially viable. Serves up to 500,000 Rwandans, growing Kigali's water capacity by approximately one third.
items.waterL: Kanzenze, Ntarama Sector, Bugesera District, Rwanda
items.waterC: Rwanda Government / Kigali Water Limited — Metito Subsidiary
items.landT: Rwanda National Land Use Master Plan
items.landD: Led by the Rwanda Land Management and Use Authority (RLMUA), under the Ministry of Environment. Consortium partners: Tzamir Architects & Planners Ltd (Israel, led by Prof. Tzamir, who also developed the Uganda National Master Plan) and Horwath HTL Rwanda (hospitality & real estate advisory). Period: November 2019 – March 2020 (revision and update). Comprehensive spatial plan covering urbanization, settlement, housing, agriculture, environment, tourism, transport, and utilities — aligned with Rwanda Vision 2050 and NST1. Cabinet approved 29 July 2020. Presidential Order No. 038/01 of 20 May 2022 gave it legal force. Aims Capital reviewed and updated the entire policy and legal framework for land use, expropriation, investment regulation, environmental management, and the secular economy. Aims Capital also drafted the Presidential Order for legal enforcement.
items.cdmD: Review of over 50 Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) investment projects with $610M total value for UNDP, aligned to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), Kyoto Protocol and Article 6 Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM) and Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) of the Paris Agreement. Included verification, prospectus and pitch-book development for COP28 (Dubai, November 2023). Projects aligned to UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement Article 6 VCM/NDC.
items.ewsaD: Commissioned by the Rwanda Government under World Bank funding. Led to formation of Rwanda Energy Group (REG) and Water and Sanitation Corporation (WASAC Ltd, established 2014). Aims Capital drafted governance instruments, managed asset separation of energy and water utilities, and supported senior recruitment for both entities.
items.finD: Co-developed Rwanda's Five-Year Sustainable Finance Roadmap (2022–2029) for Kigali International Financial Centre (KIFC) / UNDP. GBRW (UK-based financial sector regulatory advisory) conducted the diagnostic: stakeholder analysis at macro/meso/micro level, benchmarking against peer African jurisdictions, and SWOT analysis of banking, capital markets, and insurance sectors. Garnet Partners also contributed. Two strategic pillars: Scaling Sustainable Finance and Making Finance Sustainable. Launched 26 October 2022, officiated by Minister of State for National Treasury Richard Tusabe. The Roadmap has since attracted EUR 300M+ in climate finance commitments from AFD, EIB, IFC, and KfW (announced June 2023 at the Paris Summit for a New Global Financing Pact).
items.wasteD: Commissioned by the African Development Bank (2017). Conducted jointly with Planet Partnerships across Rwanda, Ethiopia and Algeria. Study covered waste management and circular economy frameworks, providing recommendations for sustainable waste infrastructure in pilot African countries.
items.aviD: Advisory services for Avia Group (Lithuania-based aircraft leasing, sale/purchase, crew staffing, MRO, and ground-handling), Rwanda Air, and Nexus Group (Saudi Arabia-based airline operating systems). Aims Capital holds a Service Level Agreement with Nexus Group for aviation technology and operations collaboration across Africa.
items.houseD: Advisory and support services for affordable housing projects: 165 units in Nyanza, Southern Province, and 180 units in Rwamagana District, Eastern Province. Advisory scope included legal compliance, architectural coordination, and contract management.
items.zhongD: Zhong Tong is China's largest manufacturer of buses, including electric buses and charging infrastructure. Aims Capital signed a formal representation agreement, appointed as Zhong Tong's representative for green transport promotion across Africa. Agreement signed in Kigali.
